newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Typhoon delays Filipino satellite launch.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon delays Filipino satellite launch.

text.p: The launch of a Philippine communications satellite has been deferred for a third time because of a typhoon heading towards Fujian province in China, site of the tracking station for the launch.
In a statement on Tuesday, the Mabuhay Philippine Satellite Corp, owner and operator of the satellite, said the launch has been rescheduled for August 21.
China had originally planned the launch between August 8-10 and it was deferred to August 10-12. Bad weather further delayed the launch to August 19.
Mabuhay said the tracking station will monitor the separation of the rocket from the satellite which will then travel to its orbital slot.
The "Agila" satellite will be the first to be launched by a Filipino-led consortium.

Mabuhay is a consortium of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co , Pilipino Telephone Corp, Philippines Communications Satellite Corp, Pasifik Nusanatara, Cable Entertainment Corp, Philippine Satellite Corp, Republic Broadcasting Corp and China Everbright Group Ltd.
